data.title: Alleged Member of “8-Digits Team” Ransomware Group Extradited from Italy for Role in Major Data Extortion Campaign Against U.S. Hospitals, Healthcare Entities, and Schools
data.summary: Roman Khlynovskiy, 43, a Kazak national, made his initial appearance in Knoxville, Tennessee, federal court today after being extradited from Italy to face charges for his alleged role in a ransomware and extortion conspiracy that targeted U.S. schools, hospitals, and healthcare entities.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/alleged-m.label: Alleged Member of “8-Digits Team” Ransomware Group Extradited from Italy for Role in Major Data Extortion Campaign Against U.S. Hospitals, Healthcare Entities, and Schools

data.title: Joint Statement from Department of Commerce and Department of Justice on Megaspeed Investigation
data.summary: The Department of Commerce and the Department of Justice are providing the public with an update on the investigation of the Singaporean company Megaspeed, which has attracted significant public attention in the last week. While we don’t typically comment on ongoing investigations, it is in the public interest to provide the facts and address inaccurate information circulating in public reporting.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/joint-sta.label: Joint Statement from Department of Commerce and Department of Justice on Megaspeed Investigation

data.title: PACE Organization InnovAge Agrees to Pay $36M to Resolve False Claims Act Allegations of Failing to Provide Comprehensive Medical Services and Timely Specialist Referrals to Seniors
data.summary: InnovAge Holding Corporation (InnovAge), headquartered in Denver, Colorado, has agreed to pay a total of $36 million to resolve allegations that it violated the federal False Claims Act and state laws by failing to provide required comprehensive medical services and timely referrals to medical specialists as expeditiously as its patients’ health conditions required.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/pace-orga.label: PACE Organization InnovAge Agrees to Pay $36M to Resolve False Claims Act Allegations of Failing to Provide Comprehensive Medical Services and Timely Specialist Referrals to Seniors

data.title: Salinas Man Sentenced to Over 11 Years in Prison for Attempted Sexual Exploitation of a 12-Year-Old and Distributing Child Pornography
data.summary: Donald Ramirez, 40, of Salinas, California, was sentenced to 138 months in prison and 15 years of supervised release for attempted enticement and coercion of a minor and for distribution of child pornography. He was also ordered to pay $72,000 in restitution.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/salinas-m.label: Salinas Man Sentenced to Over 11 Years in Prison for Attempted Sexual Exploitation of a 12-Year-Old and Distributing Child Pornography

data.title: Justice Department, VA, and VA OIG Announce Enforcement Actions Against 15 Defendants for Defrauding Veterans Benefits Programs
data.summary: The Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division, along with the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), and VA Office of Inspector General today announced a nationwide series of enforcement actions targeting VA benefit fraud and related offenses amid National Veterans Awareness Week.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/justice-d.label: Justice Department, VA, and VA OIG Announce Enforcement Actions Against 15 Defendants for Defrauding Veterans Benefits Programs

data.title: Mississippi Businessman Sentenced to 10 Years in Prison for $19M Medicare Fraud
data.summary: A Mississippi businessman was sentenced yesterday to 10 years in prison for paying illegal kickbacks for fraudulent doctors’ orders and then using those orders to fraudulently bill Medicare over $19 million through seven different durable medical equipment (DME) supply companies.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/mississip.label: Mississippi Businessman Sentenced to 10 Years in Prison for $19M Medicare Fraud

data.title: Child Predator Deemed “Extreme Danger” Sentenced to Life in Prison For Relentlessly Sexually Exploiting Multiple Minors in Hawaii
data.summary: Darren Patrick Riley, 46, of Honolulu, Hawaii, was sentenced to life in prison by Senior U.S. District Judge J. Michael Seabright following his conviction by a jury of 12 counts related to his trafficking and sexual exploitation of five minor boys in Oahu in 2019 and 2020.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/child-pre.label: Child Predator Deemed “Extreme Danger” Sentenced to Life in Prison For Relentlessly Sexually Exploiting Multiple Minors in Hawaii

data.title: Iranian Intelligence Agent Sentenced to Over 27 Years in Prison for Foiled Plot to Assassinate U.S. Government Officials
data.summary: Earlier today, in federal court in Brooklyn, Asif Merchant, 48, of Pakistan, was sentenced by U.S. District Judge Eric R. Komitee to 330 months in prison for attempting to commit an act of terrorism transcending national boundaries and murder for hire.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/iranian-i.label: Iranian Intelligence Agent Sentenced to Over 27 Years in Prison for Foiled Plot to Assassinate U.S. Government Officials

data.title: Tajik National Convicted of Providing Material Support to ISIS and Firearms Offenses
data.summary: A federal jury in Brooklyn today convicted Mansuri Manuchekhri, also known as “Mansuri Manchekhri” and “Manysher,” on four counts of an indictment charging him with conspiring to provide material support to the Islamic State of Iraq and al-Sham (ISIS) and the Islamic State-Khorasan Province (ISIS-K), conspiring to possess and possessing firearms and ammunition while unlawfully in the United States, and making false statements to federal agents.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/tajik-nat.label: Tajik National Convicted of Providing Material Support to ISIS and Firearms Offenses

data.title: Justice Department Surpasses $1B In Awards Under Reauthorized Radiation Exposure Compensation Act
data.summary: The Justice Department announced today that it has awarded more than $1 billion in compassionate compensation to newly eligible claimants under the recently reauthorized Radiation Exposure Compensation Act (RECA).

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/justice-d.label: Justice Department Surpasses $1B In Awards Under Reauthorized Radiation Exposure Compensation Act

data.title: Pharmacy Owner Sentenced to 82 Months in Prison for $5.6M Health Care Fraud Scheme and Illegal Distribution of Oxycodone
data.summary: A Michigan pharmacy owner was sentenced yesterday to 82 months in prison with three years’ supervised release for a $5.6 million health care fraud scheme and for illegally distributing oxycodone. The defendant has been detained since October 7, after his arrest for violating his bond conditions.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/pharmacy-.label: Pharmacy Owner Sentenced to 82 Months in Prison for $5.6M Health Care Fraud Scheme and Illegal Distribution of Oxycodone

data.title: Russian National Indicted for Acting as a Foreign Agent of Russia to Target Silicon Valley Technology and Defense Company
data.summary: A federal grand jury has indicted Igor D’iu, a Russian national, on charges of conspiring to act as an agent of a foreign government, acting as an agent of a foreign government without notice to the Attorney General, interstate stalking, and fraud in connection with identification documents, all in connection with an alleged scheme to conduct surveillance and gather information about employees of a Silicon Valley technology and defense company.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/russian-n.label: Russian National Indicted for Acting as a Foreign Agent of Russia to Target Silicon Valley Technology and Defense Company

data.title: Texas-Based Company Pleads Guilty to Trafficking Deadly Synthetic Opioids
data.summary: A business-to-business online marketplace headquartered in Texas — eWorldTrade LLC — pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to distribute synthetic opioids for unlawful importation into the United States and agreed to pay a criminal fine of $1,350,000 based on its ability to pay.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/texas-bas.label: Texas-Based Company Pleads Guilty to Trafficking Deadly Synthetic Opioids

data.title: Maryland Man Sentenced to 27 Years in Prison for Sex Trafficking Two Adult Women
data.summary: Brandon Sartor, 33, of Prince George’s County, Maryland, was sentenced to 27 years in prison and ordered to pay $239,800 in restitution for sex trafficking two adult women using force, fraud, or coercion.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/maryland-.label: Maryland Man Sentenced to 27 Years in Prison for Sex Trafficking Two Adult Women

data.title: Peruvian National Sentenced in Transnational Government Imposter Scheme that Defrauded Thousands of U.S. Consumers
data.summary: Carla Magaly Alcedo Mendoza (Alcedo), 45, of Lima, Peru, was sentenced today to eight years in prison and three years of supervised release for overseeing a years-long transnational fraud conspiracy that used government impersonation tactics to defraud thousands of consumers across the United States.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/peruvian-.label: Peruvian National Sentenced in Transnational Government Imposter Scheme that Defrauded Thousands of U.S. Consumers

data.title: “Lows” Gang Member Sentenced to 10 Years in Prison For His Participation in a RICO Conspiracy
data.summary: A federal judge sentenced Deontae Jackson, 37, of Minneapolis to 10 years in prison for his role in a Racketeering Influenced Corrupt Organization (RICO) conspiracy that included violence and fentanyl distribution.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/lows-gang.label: “Lows” Gang Member Sentenced to 10 Years in Prison For His Participation in a RICO Conspiracy

data.title: Louisiana Woman Convicted of Fraud, Obstruction, and Money Laundering in Nearly $10M Tax Refund Scheme
data.summary: A federal jury in the Western District of Louisiana convicted Jane Frances Pierce, 64, of Boyce, Louisiana, of mail fraud, filing false tax returns, corruptly interfering with an IRS investigation, and money laundering.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/louisiana.label: Louisiana Woman Convicted of Fraud, Obstruction, and Money Laundering in Nearly $10M Tax Refund Scheme

data.title: Federal Court Dismisses Challenge to National Security Exemption for Energy Development in Gulf of America
data.summary: The U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia dismissed a lawsuit earlier this week challenging the first national security exemption ever issued pursuant to the Endangered Species Act. The exemption terminated litigation threatening oil and gas in the Gulf of America — a critical source of domestic production. The court held that it lacked jurisdiction because Congress directed all challenges to the Committee’s exemption decisions to the federal courts of appeals, not the district courts.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/federal-c.label: Federal Court Dismisses Challenge to National Security Exemption for Energy Development in Gulf of America

data.title: Michigan Home Health Care Agency Owner Sentenced to 4 Years in Prison for $1.6M Medicare Fraud Scheme Fueled by Illegal Kickbacks
data.summary: A Michigan nurse and home health agency owner was sentenced today to 4 years in prison for a $1.6 million scheme to defraud Medicare. She was also ordered to pay $1,652,130.67 in restitution to Medicare, and to pay $1,652,130.67 in forfeiture.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/michigan-.label: Michigan Home Health Care Agency Owner Sentenced to 4 Years in Prison for $1.6M Medicare Fraud Scheme Fueled by Illegal Kickbacks

data.title: 3 Mexican Nationals Plead Guilty to Laundering Millions of Dollars in Drug Proceeds from the United States to Mexico
data.summary: Three Mexican nationals pleaded guilty for their roles in the collection of millions in drug proceeds in the United States and the return of those proceeds via cryptocurrency or wire transfers to Mexico as part of a money laundering conspiracy.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/3-mexican.label: 3 Mexican Nationals Plead Guilty to Laundering Millions of Dollars in Drug Proceeds from the United States to Mexico

data.title: Kansas Realtor Indicted for Tax Evasion, Failure to File Tax Returns, and Pandemic Relief Fraud
data.summary: A federal grand jury in Kansas City, Kansas, returned a superseding indictment yesterday charging a Louisburg, Kansas, woman with tax evasion, wire fraud, and willful failure to file personal and corporate income tax returns.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/kansas-re.label: Kansas Realtor Indicted for Tax Evasion, Failure to File Tax Returns, and Pandemic Relief Fraud

data.title: Justice Department Secures Permanent Injunction Against California Laws Restricting Federal Law Enforcement Operations
data.summary: The United States District Judge Christina A. Snyder of the United States District Court for the Central District of California entered a permanent injunction prohibiting the State of California, Gavin Newsom in his official capacity as Governor of California, and Rob Bonta in his official capacity as Attorney General of California, from enforcing California laws regulating federal law enforcement officers and agencies. The order permanently enjoins enforcement of Sections 7288 and 7289 of the California Government Code and Sections 185.5 and 13654 of the California Penal Code against the United States, federal law enforcement officers, and federal law enforcement agencies. The court entered the permanent injunction as part of a final resolution of the United States' lawsuit challenging California's unconstitutional attempt to regulate federal law enforcement operations.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/justice-d.label: Justice Department Secures Permanent Injunction Against California Laws Restricting Federal Law Enforcement Operations

data.title: Federal Jury Convicts Fifth Defendant for Scheme to Assassinate Haitian President Jovenel Moïse in Homeland Security Task Force Investigation
data.summary: A federal jury in Miami convicted a fifth defendant for his role in the July 7, 2021, assassination of Haitian President Jovenel Moïse.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/federal-j.label: Federal Jury Convicts Fifth Defendant for Scheme to Assassinate Haitian President Jovenel Moïse in Homeland Security Task Force Investigation

data.title: Northeast Georgia Man Charged with International Money Laundering and Destroying Evidence Tied to ISIS
data.summary: A Lavonia, Georgia, resident is in federal custody charged by criminal complaint with international money laundering and destruction of evidence following an FBI investigation into allegations of sending more than $26,000 to individuals and groups affiliated with a designated foreign terrorist organization, the Islamic State of Iraq and al Sham (ISIS).

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/northeast.label: Northeast Georgia Man Charged with International Money Laundering and Destroying Evidence Tied to ISIS
